global_rules: One task = one commit. Conventional commit prefixed with the task ID, e.g. 'fix(test): [CR-A1] dispose engine in conftest teardown'.
Never add a bare 'except Exception' that returns a default value. Failures propagate or return an explicit typed error.
Never add a suppression comment (# inversion:ok, # type: ignore, # noqa) without a same-line task-ID reference AND a test proving the suppressed condition is safe.
Never set an attribute to None on import failure. Either the import succeeds or construction fails loudly.
Never delete or weaken a test to make a gate pass. That is a HUMAN-GATE.
Never modify files outside the task's allowed_paths. Stop and report instead of widening scope.
No behavior changes in refactor tasks. If a fix requires changing business logic, stop and flag it.
Every task begins by verifying its premise still holds. If it does not, record that and close the task without inventing adjacent work.
If a gate fails after three attempts, revert to the last green commit and report. Do not keep trying variations.
Never force-push. Never rebase a pushed branch.

tasks.title: Single egress chokepoint with default-deny allowlist
design_requirements: One module all outbound HTTP passes through. Default deny.
An empty allowlist means ZERO egress, not unrestricted egress.
Host-based entries; wildcards only at the leftmost label, and logged as such.
A denied connection raises a typed explicit exception. It does NOT return None, an empty response, or a degraded result.
Enforced at the lowest practical layer (custom transport / session factory) so new call sites are denied by default.
Add a lint rule or import hook so direct requests/httpx imports fail. A guard that can be bypassed by importing directly is decorative.
Effective configuration inspectable at runtime without reading source.
tasks.exit_gate: python -m pytest tests/security/test_egress_guard.py --no-cov -q && python -m pytest tests/ --no-cov -q
required_test_cases: Denied host raises the typed exception
The exception is not swallowed anywhere on the governed path

tasks.title: Route every call site through the guard
steps: Migrate each inventoried call site to the guarded transport, including MCP client transports. Each MCP server is a second egress path that silently falsifies the one-outbound-flow claim if unguarded.
tasks.exit_gate: ! grep -rEn '^\s*(import requests|import httpx|from requests|from httpx|import aiohttp)' backend/ core/ sdk/ --include='*.py' | grep -v egress_guard.py && python -m pytest tests/ --no-cov -q

tasks.title: Rename the confidence score and stop swallowing exceptions
tasks.human_gate_reason: HD-1: Kevin picks the new name before the agent proceeds
tasks.premise: 147 lines computing C = 0.35*evidence_quality + 0.30*ka_consensus + 0.20*persona_agreement + 0.15*gate_factor. Missing evidence/KA/personas each return 0.5; missing gate decision returns 0.8; whole calculate() body wrapped in except Exception: return 0.5. 0.995 is hard-wired as the healthcare/finance/legal/safety threshold across trust_validation_gateway.py, opa_policy.py, and ~a dozen sites. A run where four subsystems silently failed is numerically indistinguishable from a genuine moderate-confidence run.
steps: Rename to a non-probabilistic name (governance_score / check_pass_ratio / Kevin's choice).

Update the docstring to describe what is actually computed; remove the 'spec Section 13' citation, which describes C = sigma(alpha*sum(w_i*e_i) - beta*conflicts - gamma*H) -- a sigmoid with conflict and entropy terms, none of which are implemented.
Remove every default-on-failure return. A missing component yields an explicit typed incomplete result naming which inputs were unavailable.
Remove the blanket except Exception.
forbidden: Implementing the sigmoid formula in this task. Changing the math before it can be measured swaps one unvalidated number for another. That is Phase F, after CR-F2 exists.
tasks.exit_gate: ! grep -rn 'except Exception' backend/truth_engine/confidence_calculator.py && ! grep -rn 'return 0\.5\|return 0\.8' backend/truth_engine/confidence_calculator.py && python -m pytest tests/ --no-cov -q

tasks.title: FIPS-capable crypto abstraction
tasks.human_gate_reason: HD-4: FIPS module choice is a procurement and platform decision
tasks.premise: EncryptionManager implements real AES-256-GCM (AESGCM.generate_key(bit_length=256), 12-byte nonce) with Fernet as the KEK wrapper -- a correct envelope design. But AES-256-GCM is a FIPS-APPROVED ALGORITHM, and the default cryptography build is NOT a FIPS-VALIDATED MODULE. Module validation, not algorithm choice, is the federal question. Same applies to Windows DPAPI as used here.
steps: Abstract the crypto provider behind an interface.
Add a FIPS-mode configuration flag.
Add a startup self-check reporting the active provider and its validation status.
Document precisely what is and is not validated. Do not overclaim.
tasks.exit_gate: Provider interface tested with at least two implementations; startup reports active provider; docs/CRYPTOGRAPHY.md states validation status without overclaiming.

tasks.title: Generate the system card from code
tasks.premise: The KA limitations pattern -- capabilities returning explicit statements of what they did NOT establish -- is the best idea in this codebase and a code-level implementation of EU AI Act Art. 13 and ISO 42001 A.8.2. Most vendors write this in a PDF nobody reads; this computes it per invocation.

GENERATE from code, not by hand -- a hand-written card drifts, and drift is what created this plan.
